findings.failure_path: Fallback mode is jq-only with realpath failing on a dangling chain. Once total_sym_hops reaches 16, the readlink loop and the parent-walk check stop without saying anything, and check_target allows the edit. The kernel resolves up to 40 symlink hops, so a chain of 17 or more links ending in an uncreated subdirectory of a .worktree-only primary checkout gets a write past the isolation guard. This breaks the fail-closed rule in hooks/AGENTS.md.
findings.smallest_fix: When the budget runs out while the current path is still a symlink, call deny with a 'symlink chain too deep' message instead of returning. Add a probe that uses a 17-hop chain together with the realpath-failing shim.

concern_results.conclusion: resolve_turn_key: invocationNum==0 always bumps seq, so new user turns get a fresh key even with the same prompt, a stale or missing transcript, or no initialNumSteps. invocationNum>0 reuses the active key unless the turn_id actually changes, and that path backfills a turn_id that was missing. Guard chained-symlink handling now walks dangling parents inside the readlink loop. Within the bounds of this diff, the acceptance criteria are met.

One-shot merge grants are not re-armed on invocationNum>0. In the guard, the shared 16-hop budget fails open: when it runs out, the walk stops silently and allows the edit, while the kernel follows up to 40 hops. See the finding.
Symlink cycles are bounded and corrupt or missing state files fall back to seq 0. When the hop budget runs out, the guard allows instead of denying (see the finding).

p6l uses a dangling intermediate directory, which makes GNU realpath fail, so the readlink loop is exercised. p6m shims realpath to always fail. The agy tests cover new turns with no initialNumSteps and turns with no transcript. EXPECTED_PROBES moves to 32. No test checks behavior at the hop-budget limit.
The changes stay within the four accepted items. REQUIRE_BASELINE and the opt-in PERF_BOUND_MS answer earlier review findings on in-scope suite wiring. The guard uses Bash 3.2-compatible constructs.
Every change is at file level and can be reverted on its own. A leftover .active.turn file without seq defaults to seq 0, so old state needs no migration.
Deny messages and suite summaries are unchanged. When the guard's hop budget runs out, it emits no diagnostic.
The claim that symlink hops are bounded to 16 is accurate, but it reads as if containment is complete. In fact chains longer than 16 hops are allowed without any notice.
Fallback mode is jq-only with realpath failing on a dangling chain. In that mode, a symlink chain longer than 16 hops (the kernel follows up to 40) gets past the primary-checkout isolation guard.

Spec evidence and a source-register row are updated. hooks/AGENTS.md requires fail-closed behavior where safety needs it, but the guard fails open when the hop budget runs out. That conflict is reported in the finding.
